title: IT Operations Management Software For Small IT Teams: What To Use For What
summary: Which IT operations management software fits a 2 to 5 person IT team? Compare tools for requests, new hires, leavers, laptops, and licenses.
body_markdown:
It's 8:40 on a Monday. A new project engineer starts at 9, and their laptop is still in a box on your desk. Their manager asked for software access in Slack, HR sent the start date by email, and a contractor who finished in June still has a login to the shared drive because nobody told you they left.


If you run IT with two to five people at a 50 to 200 person company, most of your week looks like this. It's not servers going down. It's requests, approvals, laptops, logins, and licenses, spread across inboxes and spreadsheets. This guide covers which IT operations management software handles which part of that work, and what to check before you sign off on one.


## TL;DR


- "IT operations management software" covers five very different tool types: infrastructure monitoring, service desks, device management, SaaS management, and request and access portals.
- Most "best ITOM tools" lists are written for large IT departments. A 2 to 5 person IT team spends more time on people work (new hires, leavers, access requests) than on server alerts.
- The biggest risk at this size is access that never gets removed. Ask every tool how it handles leavers before you buy.
- If HR, managers, and contractors all touch your IT process, pick a tool where they can each get their own login and only see their own records.
- You can keep your asset list in Airtable or Google Sheets and build a request portal on top, instead of migrating everything, or you can describe the portal you want in plain words, and an AI builder like Nola sets up the first version.


## What is IT operations management software?


IT operations management (ITOM) software is any tool an IT team uses to keep the company's technology running day to day. That includes the systems, the devices people work on, the software they log in to, and the requests people send to IT.


The term is broad, which is why search results for it mix very different products. A server monitoring tool, a laptop management tool, and a ticketing tool can all be called "IT operations management software", but they solve different problems. Knowing which problem you have is the first step.


## What does IT operations look like at a 50 to 200 person company?


At this size, IT is usually a small team, often reporting to an operations director or the COO. Most of the company's software is in the cloud, so there are few servers to watch. The work is mostly about people:


- **New hires:** ordering a laptop, creating accounts, adding the person to the right shared folders before day one.
- **Leavers:** removing access to every tool the same day, collecting equipment, and transferring files.
- **Access requests:** "Can Priya get edit access to the finance folder?" and the approval that should come with it.
- **Devices:** who has which laptop, phone, or site tablet, and when it's due for replacement.
- **Software licenses and vendors:** what you pay for, who uses it, and when it renews.


Leavers are where small teams get caught out. In a[2025 survey of 1,200 US workers by PasswordManager.com](https://www.passwordmanager.com/4-in-10-workers-hack-former-employer-passwords-for-personal-use/) , 40% said they had used a former employer's login after leaving. Of those, 60% said they could get in because the password had never been changed.


Software is the other moving target.[Zylo's 2026 SaaS Management Index](https://zylo.com/news/2026-saas-management-index) found that business units now control 81% of software spend, while IT directly manages 15%. In practice, that means teams sign up for tools on their own, and IT finds out when someone needs access removed.


## Which types of IT operations management software are there?


Here's how the five main tool types compare for a small IT team. Most companies end up with more than one, so the useful question is which job each tool should own.


Short on time? Monitoring and device tools handle the machines;[Noloco](https://noloco.io/) handles the requests, approvals, and access around them.


Type of tool What it does Best for Where it falls short for a 2 to 5 person IT team Examples


**Infrastructure monitoring** Watches servers, networks, and cloud services, and alerts you when something slows down or goes offline. Companies running their own servers, on-site networks, or customer-facing apps. Doesn't handle requests, approvals, new hires, or leavers. Datadog, SolarWinds, ManageEngine OpManager


**IT service desk** A ticket queue where staff log IT problems and requests, with response times and assignment. Teams handling a high, steady volume of tickets. Larger platforms can take weeks to configure. HR or managers who approve requests may need their own seat, or end up approving by email. ServiceNow, Jira Service Management, Freshservice


**Device management** Manages laptops and phones remotely: installs updates, enforces passwords, wipes lost devices. Any company with laptops leaving the office. Knows the device, not the request behind it: who asked for it, who approved it, or which contractor it was lent to. NinjaOne, Jamf, Microsoft Intune


**SaaS management** Finds which software the company pays for, who uses it, and when it renews. Companies with a long list of software subscriptions and unclear ownership. Shows what you pay for, but requests and approvals for new tools still happen in email or chat. Zylo, BetterCloud


**Spreadsheets or Airtable** Holds the asset register, license list, and new hire checklist in rows and columns. Small teams where one or two people keep the list up to date. Giving HR, managers, and contractors their own filtered view and edit rights gets harder as more people need access. Google Sheets, Excel, Airtable


**Noloco** Builds an IT request portal, asset tracker, and joiner and leaver workflow on top of Airtable, Google Sheets, or[Noloco Tables](https://noloco.io/data/noloco-tables) . IT work that involves people outside IT: HR, managers, staff, and contractors, each with[their own login and permissions](https://noloco.io/product/permissions) . Doesn't monitor servers, push updates to devices, or scan your network. Pair it with a monitoring or device management tool. Describe your IT portal to[Nola](https://noloco.io/product/nola) or start from the[team intranet](https://www.noloco.io/solutions/team-intranet)


Monitoring and device management tools do jobs no portal can do, like alerting you when a server goes down or wiping a stolen laptop. Keep them for that. The gap for most small teams is the people side: the requests, approvals, and access changes that involve HR, managers, and contractors who aren't in IT.


## What should a small IT team look for before buying?


Feature lists for IT tools are long, and most of them are built for 50 person IT departments. These are the questions that matter more when IT is two to five people:


- **Can people outside IT take part without a full license?** HR needs to submit new hires, managers need to approve access, and contractors may need to report a broken device. If each of them needs a paid seat, they will go back to email.
- **Can you control who sees which records?** A manager should see their own team's equipment, not the whole asset list. A contractor should see only their own requests. Check whether[permissions work at the record level](https://noloco.io/product/permissions) , not just by page or table.
- **What happens when someone leaves?** Look for a leaver checklist that creates the tasks automatically and shows which accounts are still open.
- **Does it work with the data you already have?** If your asset list lives in Airtable or Google Sheets, moving it can take longer than setting up the new tool.
- **Can your team change it without a consultant?** Your process will change when you add a site, a new office, or a new type of contractor. Adding a field or an approval step shouldn't need a support ticket.


Use the checklist below to compare any tool you're considering.


IT job Question to ask any tool Red flag


**New hire setup** Can HR submit a new starter and trigger the laptop order and account setup tasks for IT? HR still has to email IT with the start date.


**Leaver access removal** When someone leaves, does it list every account and device linked to them, with a task for each? IT has to remember which tools the person used.


**Access requests** Can a manager approve a request from their own login, with the approval saved on the record? Approvals happen in Slack and can't be found later.


**Laptops and equipment** Can each person see the devices assigned to them, and can managers see only their team's? Everyone sees the whole asset list, or nobody outside IT sees any of it.


**Software licenses** Does it show who uses each tool and remind you before a renewal date? Renewals show up as a surprise charge on the company card.


**Contractors and partners** Can external people log in and see only their own requests and equipment? Contractors share a staff login or get added to the internal tool with full access.


**Reporting to leadership** Can you show open requests, overdue leaver tasks, and license spend without building a spreadsheet each month? Every report starts with an export.


## Where do spreadsheets and Airtable fit in IT operations?


Many small IT teams already run their asset register, license list, and new hire checklist in Google Sheets or Airtable. That's a reasonable starting point. The data is structured, the team knows how to use it, and it costs little.


It starts to get harder when more people need to use it. HR wants to add new starters, managers want to see their team's devices, and you don't want either of them editing the license list. Airtable's interfaces help, but giving five different groups five different views of the same records takes more work as the company grows.


You don't have to migrate to fix this. One option is to keep Airtable as the place your data lives and[add a portal on top of it](https://noloco.io/data/airtable) , so each group gets its own login, form, and filtered view. If you're weighing a bigger change, this[comparison of Noloco and Airtable interfaces](https://noloco.io/noloco-vs-airtable-interfaces) covers where each one fits.


## How can a small IT team build its own IT operations portal?


An IT operations portal is one place where staff send requests, HR submits new hires and leavers, managers approve access, and IT sees everything that's open. Here's how to set one up in Noloco without moving your data:


1. **Connect your existing data.** Link your asset list and license list from Airtable, Google Sheets, or another source through[Noloco's integrations](https://noloco.io/integrations) , or start fresh in Noloco Tables.
2. **Describe what you need.** Tell[Nola](https://noloco.io/product/nola) , Noloco's AI builder, something like "an IT request portal where staff log equipment and access requests, and managers approve them." It builds the first version, which you can then adjust.
3. **Add request forms.** Set up[forms](https://noloco.io/product/forms) for new hires, leavers, access requests, and broken equipment, so every request arrives with the details you need.
4. **Set roles and permissions.** Staff see their own requests and devices. Managers see their team. HR sees joiners and leavers. IT sees everything.
5. **Automate the leaver steps.** Use[workflows](https://noloco.io/product/workflows) so that when HR marks someone as leaving, IT gets a task for every account and device linked to that person.


To be clear about the limits: Noloco doesn't monitor servers, push software updates to laptops, or scan your network. Keep a monitoring or device management tool for that. Noloco handles the part those tools leave to email: who asked for what, who approved it, and what still needs to be done. For a ready-made starting point, see this[IT team intranet built on Airtable](https://noloco.io/build/team-intranet-airtable-it) .


## Final thoughts


The right IT operations management software for a small IT team isn't the one with the longest feature list. It's the setup that makes sure a new hire has a working laptop on day one, a leaver loses access the day they leave, and you can answer "who has access to this?" without checking five places.


Start with the job that causes the most chasing today. For most teams that's joiners and leavers. Fix that first, then add asset tracking and license renewals once the basics run without you.

## Frequently asked questions


**What is the difference between ITOM and ITSM?**


IT operations management (ITOM) is about keeping systems, devices, and software running. IT service management (ITSM) is about how IT handles requests and incidents from the people it supports, usually through a service desk. Many small teams need a bit of both, and some tools cover parts of each.


**Can Noloco replace ITSM or IT operations management software?**


Noloco helps IT teams build custom apps and portals for the way they manage IT operations. You can create a central place for IT requests, equipment tracking, onboarding workflows, and access approvals, using the data your team already has. It’s a flexible option for teams that need more than spreadsheets but don’t want to take on a complex new platform.


**Is Noloco suitable for a small IT team in a 100-person company?**


Yes. You don’t need a large IT department to build a system that keeps your operations organized. With Noloco, a small IT team can create tools to manage equipment, handle employee requests, and coordinate onboarding and offboarding — without relying on manual updates across spreadsheets, emails, and separate tools.


**Can we manage employee onboarding and offboarding with Noloco?**


Yes. Build a workflow that guides each step, assigns tasks to the right people, and shows what’s still outstanding. For offboarding, your team can record access removals, equipment returns, and task completion in one place. Your team stays organized, and there’s a clear record of what’s been done.


**Can we manage IT assets without relying on spreadsheets?**


Yes. Build an asset management app on top of your existing data to track devices, software licenses, assigned employees, and equipment returns. Give IT, HR, and managers access to the information they need, without exposing everything to everyone. You can start with a simple asset list and adapt it as your needs grow.


**Can we build an IT request portal with custom approval workflows?**


Yes. Give employees a central place to submit IT requests, such as access changes, new equipment, or software installations. Route requests to the right approver, assign follow-up tasks, and let employees check progress without chasing your team for updates. You can shape the workflow around your existing approval process.


**Can Noloco help us manage access and permissions?**


Yes. Control what employees, managers, IT staff, and external users can see and change in your app. This is useful when several teams need to work with the same information but shouldn’t all have the same access. Noloco lets you build around your organization's roles and processes, with permissions that help keep sensitive data in the right hands.


**Do we need developers to build our own IT tools?**


No. Noloco combines AI-assisted app building with no-code tools, so your IT team can describe what it needs and build a working app without starting from scratch with code. You can build on your existing data, adapt workflows as requirements change, and spend less time waiting for development resources.
